note: Monday A, workplace English（职场英语）: 事 si6 ×3, then BBC 6 Minute English “Is it OK to disagree?” (~6 min). Hard recall only — five cards, two tiny sets (recap / off your plate / frazzled, then the done thing / miffed). One-keyword cue; say it aloud before you flip. Then a short workplace read and one Point → Reason → Example. No new cards.

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: say 事 (si6, low flat tone 低平调) three times in a row. Low and flat, not mid like 試 si3, and not falling like 時 si4.
tasks.script: 事 si6 · 事 si6 · 事 si6 (compare: 試 si3 is mid-level; 時 si4 falls; 事 si6 sits lower and stays flat)

tasks.title: BBC 6 Minute English: “Is it OK to disagree?” (ep-260101)

lines.text: Just to recap: I’ll send the draft by noon, and you’ll review it tomorrow.
lines.gloss: recap = say the agreed points before you stop.
lines.translation: 先复述一下：我中午前发草稿，你明天看。

lines.text: I’m a bit frazzled. Could you take the follow-up off my plate?
lines.gloss: frazzled = too many things at once. Off my plate = please handle this task.
lines.translation: 我这边事情堆在一起。这件事请你接手。

lines.text: If you feel miffed, is it the done thing to reply-all?
lines.gloss: miffed = slightly annoyed. The done thing = what people expect in that situation.
lines.translation: 有点恼火时，回复全部人算约定俗成吗？

tasks.prompt: One short workplace answer. Order: Point → Reason → Example. Use one phrase from today’s five cards. Say it aloud, then check the script.
tasks.script:
Point: I’ll keep the reply short and calm.
Reason: I’m frazzled, and a long email would sound sharper than I mean.
Example: Just to recap: I’ll send the draft by noon, and we can talk tomorrow.

questions.q: Tone number for 事 in 有咩事呀？
questions.explain: 事 si6, low flat. Not 試 si3 (mid) and not 時 si4 (falling).

questions.q: When you explain a work point, the order is…
questions.explain: 先结论，再原因，再一个例子。

questions.q: Fill in: Just to ___: I’ll send the draft by noon.
questions.explain: Just to recap = say the agreed points before the meeting ends.

options: Pass a task from your workload to someone else.
Clear the papers off your desk.
questions.explain: It means handing a task to someone else to deal with.
Slightly annoyed — lighter than angry. “The done thing” is what people expect you to do.
